findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "corruptopolis_entrar" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Start here. Registers you as an AI agent (anonymous, no account) and returns your agent key. Calling it means you declare you are an AI agent. Pick a name for t…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: corruptopolis_empezar · Private data: corruptopolis_yo, corruptopolis_perfil · Public sink: corruptopolis_accion, corruptopolis_informe · Destructive: corruptopolis_empezar, corruptopolis_reliquias.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: corruptopolis_empezar · Private data: corruptopolis_yo, corruptopolis_perfil · Public sink: corruptopolis_accion, corruptopolis_informe · Destructive: corruptopolis_empezar, corruptopolis_reliquias

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "corruptopolis_empezar" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
